sections.title: Name and host plant
sections.text: Puccinia emaculata Schwein. is a microscopic grass rust (Pucciniales, Pucciniaceae). The molecular revision of rust fungi on Panicum by Demers et al. (2017) retains P. capillare, witchgrass, as a confirmed host of the strict P. emaculata concept. Several rusts found on switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) and formerly called P. emaculata were separated as distinct species, including P. amari, P. novopanici and P. pammelii. Some later reports nevertheless retained the P. emaculata identification on switchgrass, so that host association should be treated cautiously.

sections.title: Symptoms and spores
sections.text: The rust forms small cinnamon-brown pustules or sori, often elongated or aligned near the veins, on leaves and sometimes stems. Uredinia produce single-celled urediniospores with finely echinulate walls. Telia, reported especially in late summer, contain dark-brown, oblong to ellipsoid teliospores divided into two cells. These microscopic characters, together with the host and DNA sequences, help distinguish related rusts; pustule colour alone is not sufficient.

sections.title: Life cycle and uncertainties
sections.text: Uredinial and telial stages are documented on grasses. The aecial stage and an alternate host have not been securely established for P. emaculata in the strict sense. Older references suggested Euphorbiaceae as alternate hosts, but this association is not confirmed for the strict concept. Molecular work demonstrated alternation between Euphorbia corollata and Panicum virgatum in Puccinia pammelii, a different switchgrass rust; these taxa should not be confused.

sections.title: Scope of this entry
sections.text: This is a plant pathogen, not a mushroom for collection. The visual description is indicative: species-level identification of rust fungi may require spore examination, host study and molecular comparison, especially within the Panicum rust complex.
